messages:
kate-support: Heads-up — customer on iOS 17 sees SSE stream drop ~30s into long-completion. They get partial JSON then a client reconnection. Logs show a 401 right before disconnect.

jules: oof. do we have the request/headers + token rotation timing?

kate-support: sent a repro app snippet and server logs. token TTL is 300s, but client SDK refreshes at 270s. This happens at ~32s into response for a 60s completion.

sam: can you paste the exact server error?

kate-support: ``ERROR: auth: token expired while handling stream; websocket sse: client disconnect (code=1006)`` plus this in request log: `Authorization: Bearer <redacted>` then `401 token invalid` after 30s.

maria: interesting — token expiry mid-stream shouldn't abort if we accept fingerprinted auth. We usually allow a request to complete even if token rotates for long-lived SSE. Which deployment are they on? hosted or dedicated?

kate-support: hosted. customer using our JS client 2.1.1 (browser SDK with keepalive), iOS WKWebView. They say backgrounding app doesn't happen.

jules: likely a client-side library bug where it re-auths and closes underlying connection then reopens without finishing stream. Can we repro with curl or a simple node SSE client while we inspect?

client-eng: repro steps from customer attached: 1) open stream POST /v1/streams with long prompt (-> ~60s), 2) watch for Authorization rotation at 30s (their system rotates tokens every 30s), 3) stream emits partial JSON then connection closed. They confirmed immediate reconnect resumes a new request (duplicate billing).

sam: can we confirm server behavior when auth fails mid-request? Should we 1) continue serving the already-accepted connection until completion, or 2) treat 401 during stream as terminal? Our current infra treats token validation only at request start, but edge proxies may enforce revalidation on keepalives.

infra-bot: deploy-check: no recent proxy changes. Edge auth middleware version v3.4.1. Known issue: proxy closes connections when upstream token cache invalidates if revalidation enabled.

maria: ok — two vectors: client rotates token (closing socket) OR proxy enforces revalidation and kills connection. Ask customer for packet capture? Also ask SDK team if 2.1.1 calls `Authorization` set on followup subrequests.

kate-support: asked for HAR and network logs. Meanwhile workaround suggestion: pin token TTL > expected response duration or use delegated static key for long-running streams. Sent workaround and asked to confirm billing refund if duplicate charges happen.

jules: also add repro with a short-lived token server that rotates every 20s so we can reproduce internally. I'll spin a local token rotation harness and run node client + our edge locally.

sam: if proxy is to blame we need a config toggle to disable mid-stream revalidation. filing infra issue now.

maria: please include these items in triage ticket: - HAR/network logs - SDK version + exact header behavior - whether connection closed client or server side (TCP FIN vs RST) - billing impact evidence (duplicated request ids)

kate-support: noted. Customer sent a HAR and TCP log showing TCP RST from server IP at the time of 401. I've attached the pcap to the ticket.

client-eng: with pcap we can see who initiated RST. If server IP sent RST we likely closed connection. will correlate with proxy logs.

sam: created INFRA-1229 with priority P1 and linked the support ticket. Assigning to eng-infra oncall.

kate-support: thanks all — I'll update customer with ETA and keep refunds on standby. :thumbsup:

jules: quick note — suggest we add a short doc to support playbook: "long-running streams and token rotation" with recommended TTL/refresh strategy and SDK guidance.

maria: agreed. will draft after root cause confirmed.

kate-support: closing loop for now, will post updates in thread when infra responds.
